newsitem.title: INDIA: India opens coal, lignite mining to private firms.
newsitem.headline: India opens coal, lignite mining to private firms.

text.p: The Indian government said on Tuesday it will propose allowing Indian companies to mine coal and lignite for captive consumption and sale.
The government said in a statement that it would move a bill in parliament to amend the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act 1973 to open up coal and lignite mining to private firms.
It said the government had decided to deregulate the prices and distribution of D-grade of non-coking coal, hard coke and soft coke with immediate effect.
The government has decided to allow state-owned Coal India Ltd and Singaremi Collieries Co Ltd to fix the prices of E, F and G grades of non-coking coal until January 1, 2000.

The government decided to amend the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act 1957 and to frame rules for the setting up of an independent body to step up the exploration of coal and lignite resources, and to allocate blocks on the basis of a competitive bidding process, the statement said.
